Report LBNL-5342E, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, December 2011. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue for ready mixed, masonry-unit and precast concrete plants; nearly all numbers are reprinted from other works. Main file (19 examples): Tables 3-5 plant energy by end use from the PCA survey (Marceau et al. 2007) for the boiler (batch-water heating at RMC plants; curing steam at precast plants), CMU curing kiln with boiler, building heat, light trucks and throughout-plant electricity, loaded per m3 of concrete from the per-yd3 columns with explicit conversion formulas (the per-ton columns are the same numbers divided by 1.96 or 1.53 and were not loaded); curing energy with high- vs low-pressure steam (0.712 vs 0.593 GJ/m3, Kawai et al. 2005, carrier not stated, loaded as target fuel); electricity of dense-phase, dilute-phase and mechanical cement conveying (Biege et al. 1998); a gas-engine CHP case at an Ontario concrete pipe plant (capacity, heat-to-power, capex and maintenance in CAD, price year not stated); absorption vs electric centrifugal chiller energy per unit of cooling. _measures.csv: every measure in Sect. 4-6 with a printed saving, cost or payback (case studies included). _other-values.csv: Table 2 industry energy (TBtu, incl. primary), plant totals, literature ranges (50-700 MJ/m3 in cold climates), conveying cost ratios, sector statistics. Not loaded: Table 6 lighting efficacies, Table 1 state production, Figures 1-3 (charts only), water and material measures without energy numbers. Traps: Table 5 column headers are scrambled by the PDF text layer (order is light trucks, industrial boiler, building heat, various equipment, throughout plant); Day & Campbell gas saving printed in yd3; footnote text on p.11 says 57% fuel and 53% electricity (sums >100%). Data are U.S. except the CHP case (Canada) and Kawai et al. (Japan).
